COLREG RULE 10 • MCA MGN 364 (M+F) AMENDMENT 2

TSS Training • Vessels under 20 metres

Training vessel: Suilven • 14.2 m • power-driven. This beginner module is written for recreational vessels under 20 m. Rule 10(j) therefore applies throughout: do not impede the safe passage of a power-driven vessel following a traffic lane. Learn the geometry first, then apply it under traffic pressure. The locked collision engine remains untouched.

HEADING, NOT COG

Correct crossing with tidal set

The vessel's heading is as nearly as practicable at right angles to traffic flow. Tide may visibly skew the track/course over ground.

COMMON ERROR

Incorrect diagonal heading

A deliberately diagonal heading makes the crossing intention less clear and does not satisfy the right-angle-heading requirement merely because the vessel eventually reaches the other side.

JOIN / LEAVE

Do not confuse crossing with joining

When joining or leaving a lane, do so at as small an angle to the general direction of traffic flow as practicable. A crossing should cross the entire lane without stopping except in emergency.

STEP 1 • OWN VESSEL

Vessel status

Select how your training vessel is being propelled. The encounter library updates automatically.

Machinery is propelling the vessel, so she is treated as a power-driven vessel.
SAILING RULE LOGIC

Sailing mode means the vessel is under sail and her propelling machinery is not being used. If machinery is used for propulsion, she is treated as power-driven even if sails remain set. Rule 13 overtaking, Rules 9/10, and other applicable rules can override the simple power-v-sail hierarchy.

NO COACHING • REAL SIMULATOR

Practical collision assessment

Select an encounter. Project Watch switches the existing simulator to EXAM mode. No tutorial coaching is provided; the normal simulator debrief records the outcome, action timing, closest approach and manoeuvre-quality flags.

Assessment rule: A collision or clearly dangerous outcome is safety-critical. Project Watch simulator scores are training metrics, not legal determinations or MCA certification.
Assessment basis: International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea (COLREGs), current MCA Master (Code vessels <200 GT) / OOW (Yachts <500 GT) oral syllabus, current MCA Small Ships Navigation and Radar assessment criteria, and current MCA examination structure. Project Watch questions are independently written and do not reproduce RYA or MCA examination questions.

2. COLREGS layer

Rule 5Rule 7Rule 8Rule 11Rule 15Rule 16Rule 17
Scenario facts established before the exercise Two power-driven vessels, in sight of one another, on unaltered crossing tracks that intersect. At handover the target is on Suilven's starboard side.
Rule 15 — crossing situation In this constructed encounter, Suilven is the vessel that has the other power-driven vessel on her starboard side and is therefore the vessel required to keep out of the way. Where circumstances admit, she should avoid crossing ahead.
Rule 16 — give-way vessel The give-way vessel must take early and substantial action to keep well clear.
Rule 8 — avoiding action Avoiding action must be assessed in the circumstances of the encounter; Project Watch does not treat one fixed helm order or one universal CPA as automatically correct.

Source baseline: IMO Collision Regulations Convention (COLREGS), current 2026 publication/overview. This prototype uses rule summaries, not a substitute for the official publication.

3. Your watch

The 1–5 score is a provisional simulator training score, not a legal finding or professional COLREGS certification. In this build, all simulator warnings are intentionally inhibited outside 0.50 NM. It uses collision outcome, closest approach, timing and manoeuvre-quality flags. The thresholds are training parameters, not statutory COLREG limits, and remain subject to maritime review.
